```text

```

`[^@]+` means any character except an `@`.
```text

```

blocks.title: Cleaning Up User Input
bullets: Consider standardizing a name typed as `Last, First`:

blocks.title: Cleaning Up User Input Example
blocks.code:
name = input("What's your name? ").strip()
if "," in name:
    last, first = name.split(", ")
    name = f"{first} {last}"
print(f"hello, {name}")
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: Cleaning Up User Input
bullets: Using regular expressions:

blocks.title: Cleaning Up User Input Example
blocks.code:
import re

name = input("What's your name? ").strip()
matches = re.search(r"^(.+), (.+)$", name)
if matches:
    last, first = matches.groups()
    name = first + " " + last
print(f"hello, {name}")
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: Cleaning Up User Input
bullets: We can request specific groups back using `matches.group`:

blocks.title: Cleaning Up User Input Example
blocks.code:
import re

name = input("What's your name? ").strip()
matches = re.search(r"^(.+), (.+)$", name)
if matches:
    name = matches.group(2) + " " + matches.group(1)
print(f"hello, {name}")
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: Cleaning Up User Input
bullets: We can combine the search and the assignment with the walrus `:=` operator:

blocks.title: Cleaning Up User Input Example
blocks.code:
import re

name = input("What's your name? ").strip()
if matches := re.search(r"^(.+), *(.+)$", name):
    name = matches.group(2) + " " + matches.group(1)
print(f"hello, {name}")
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: Extracting User Input
bullets: Now, let's extract specific information. To extract a Twitter username from a URL:

blocks.title: Extracting User Input Example
blocks.code:
import re

url = input("URL: ").strip()

username = url.replace("https://twitter.com/", "")
print(f"Username: {username}")
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: Extracting User Input
bullets: `removeprefix` is cleaner than `replace`:

blocks.title: Extracting User Input Example
blocks.code:
import re

url = input("URL: ").strip()

username = url.removeprefix("https://twitter.com/")
print(f"Username: {username}")
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: Extracting User Input
bullets: Using `re.sub` with signature `re.sub(pattern, repl, string, count=0, flags=0)`:

blocks.title: Extracting User Input Example
blocks.code:
import re

url = input("URL: ").strip()

username = re.sub(r"^(https?://)?(www\.)?twitter\.com/", "", url)
print(f"Username: {username}")
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: Extracting User Input
bullets: Using `re.search` to be more robust:

blocks.title: Extracting User Input Example
blocks.code:
import re

url = input("URL: ").strip()

if matches := re.search(r"^https?://(?:www\.)?twitter\.com/([a-z0-9_]+)", url, re.IGNORECASE):
    print(f"Username:", matches.group(1))
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: Extracting User Input
blocks.body: The `?:` tells the interpreter it does not have to capture what is in that spot.
bullets: You can learn more in Python's documentation of [re](https://docs.python.org/3/library/re.html).
